note: Window agent p1950-p1959, 2 Nov 2026. Fixes the land the compile left to nobody (Chamdo 1951-52, Italian Somaliland 1953-59, the Indian states of 1956, French West and Equatorial Africa 1958-59) and the Białystok cells the Byelorussian SSR kept; Madhya Bharat and Travancore-Cochin drawn as constituents of India; Greenland's coast and the islands of the Republic of Indonesia kept in 1953.

region.text: Xizang: the Chamdo Region and the rest of the Tibetan land the Cliopatria Tibet shape of 1951 leaves out

events.note: 23 May 1951: the Seventeen Point Agreement ends Tibet's separate rule over central Tibet and the Chamdo Region of western Kham ('came under the control of the People's Republic of China'; the page's footnote: Central Tibet 'included the western part of Kham corresponding to the Chamdo Region'). The ledger's gain of 1951 names only U-Tsang, the Cliopatria Tibet shape of 1951, which holds none of the Chamdo cells, so after the occupation ends the dossier left about 690 Tibetan cells (the Chamdo Region and the south and east of Xizang that the shape omits) to Tibet's year-end dissolve, and they stood as nobody's land in 1951-52 until the 1953 keyframe snap of the PRC took them (339 cells in the first trial). Chamdo had been under PLA control since 19 October 1950, 'under the authority of the Qamdo Liberation Committee' and 'outside the Tibetan Government's control'.

region.text: the land inside modern Poland that the Byelorussian SSR still holds on 1 January 1950: the Białystok area and a few Lublin cells

events.note: 16 August 1945: 'a border agreement between Poland and the USSR was signed'; 'The western portion of the Byelorussian SSR was restored to Poland', and 'The Belastok Region was divided into Soviet Brest Region, Grodno Region and Polish Białystok Voivodeship'. Poland's ledger/7 names the USSR as the party that returned the Białystok area, but the cells stood with the Byelorussian SSR (its 1939 gain of Western Belarus), so 101 cells (Podlachian 88, Lublin 13) were still the Byelorussian SSR's on 1 January 1950 and stayed so to 1959. Dated 1 January 1950, the first day of this window; the true date is August 1945 (a p1940-p1949 matter, see the report).

The dossier names madhya-pradesh as successor, but no such dossier exists, so the 578 cells were released to nobody at the year-end dissolve and India never took them back (a hole in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan from 1956).

events.note: 1 November 1956: 'The Malayalam-speaking regions of the Travancore-Cochin merged with the Malabar District' of Madras State to form Kerala, and 'Devikulam-Peermade and Neyyattinkara Taluks were merged with the newly formed Kerala state'. Kerala is a state of India, but the dossier names a successor 'kerala' that has no dossier, so the land was released to nobody at the year-end dissolve (79 cells, a hole in southern India from 1956).

Travancore-Cochin's loss to madras-state has no dossier to receive it, so the cells went to nobody.

region.text: Italian Somaliland (the Somalia of today without the former British Somaliland)

events.note: 1 April 1950: the British military administration of Italian Somaliland gives way to the Italian trusteeship: 'On 1 April 1950, the Amministrazione fiduciaria italiana della Somalia (AFIS) began its rule'. The land is a UN trust territory, no state's own: it leaves British Africa here, instead of staying British until the 1953 keyframe of british-africa removes it (the compile gave it to British Africa through 1949 and nothing took it back in 1950).

region.text: Italian Somaliland (the Somalia of today without the former British Somaliland)

events.note: 1 April 1950: Italy begins to administer the Trust Territory of Somaliland: 'a United Nations Trust Territory under the administration of Italy' (UN General Assembly Resolution 289 of 21 November 1949), to independence on 1 July 1960. Drawn as occupation (hatched) of unowned land, the nearest status to a trusteeship that no dossier covers; replace it when a trust-territory dossier exists.

region.text: Italian Somaliland (the Somalia of today without the former British Somaliland)

events.note: 1 July 1960: the trusteeship ends: 'On July 1, 1960, the two territories united as planned to form the Somali Republic.' Dated in the next window so that the occupation opened by events/6 does not stay open into 1960.

region.text: the seven territories that stayed in the French Community

events.note: French Community page: the constitution of the Fifth Republic was approved 'in all of the territories except French Guinea'; the seven territories of French West Africa became autonomous states within the Community from 24 November 1958 (French Sudan), 25 November (Senegal), 28 November (Mauritania), 4 December (Dahomey and Ivory Coast), 11 December (Upper Volta) and 19 December (Niger), and 'the territories that became Community member states did not form part of the French Republic' but sat inside the Community, whose outline is the Fifth Republic's keyframe of 1958. The dossiers dissolve the federation at the year end into successors that begin in 1960, so 18,468 cells stood as nobody's land in 1958-59 and the Fifth Republic's vassal_start events of November-December 1958 (ledger/5-14) found nothing to tint. This gives the land to the Fifth Republic first, so those events then draw it in the vassal tint, as for Madagascar.

region.text: the four territories the page names (Chad, Gabon, Middle Congo, Ubangi-Shari), Wadai included

events.note: French Community page: 'Chad, Gabon, the Middle Congo' became autonomous states within the Community on 28 November 1958 and 'Ubangi-Shari' on 1 December 1958; 'the territories that became Community member states did not form part of the French Republic' but sat inside the Community, whose outline the Fifth Republic's keyframe of 1958 draws. As for French West Africa, the year-end dissolve of French Equatorial Africa left the land to nobody (9,412 cells in 1958-59); this hands it to the Fifth Republic before the vassal_start events of November-December. [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: the 100 km circle around N'Djamena (the 'Fort Lamy strip') was dropped: the page names only the four territories, the strip between the Logone and Chari lies inside Chad's polygon, and the circle only moved 2 cells west of the Logone (Kousseri side, Cameroon) from French Equatorial Africa to the Fifth Republic's direct land.]

region.text: the Greenland colony's own shape (the whole island with its coast and offshore islands), as the greenland_1945 keyframe draws it

events.note: 1953: 'Greenland's colonial status was ended and it was made an integral part of the Kingdom of Denmark'. The greenland dossier's dissolve names the country polygon of Greenland (8,192 cells) as Denmark's and so releases 155 coast and island cells of the colony's own Cliopatria shape to nobody; this takes the colony's whole shape while Greenland still holds it, so no coast is left unowned from 1953.

correction.text: the Republic of 1953-1959: the dossier's 1953 shape plus every cell of the archipelago except western New Guinea, so that the keyframe snap does not release islands the Republic held

keyframe_overrides.why: Sovereignty over 'all the territory of the former Dutch East Indies with the exception of Dutch New Guinea' passed to Indonesia on 27 December 1949 ('Sovereignty was formally transferred on 27 December 1949'). Cliopatria's 1953-59 shape omits about 80 cells held by the ledger (Maluku Utara 19, Nusa Tenggara Timur 17, Sulawesi Tengah 17 and others), which the snap of 1953 released to nobody to the end of the window; the page gives no reason to take any island out of the Republic.

rulings.why: Madhya Bharat was 'an Indian state in west-central India, created on 28 May 1948', with a Rajpramukh to 31 October 1956, and then merged into Madhya Pradesh: a state of the Indian Union, not an independent country. The size rule gives its land to the smaller Madhya Bharat in 1951-56 as a direct state; no hierarchy row ties it to India, so this draws it as India's constituent.

Travancore-Cochin was 'a short-lived state of India' formed on 1 July 1949 and ending on 1 November 1956 (Kerala and Madras State); the size rule gives it to the smaller state as a direct state, and no hierarchy row ties it to India, so this draws it as India's constituent.
